column3: Charles Taze Russell and others form a Bible study group in Pittsburgh (1870); from 1879 supporters meet as autonomous congregations, and Zion's Watch Tower Tract Society follows in 1881.
Russell moves the Society's headquarters to Brooklyn (1909); by 1910 about 50,000 people worldwide are associated with the Bible Students.
Rutherford becomes president in 1917; tens of thousands leave in the decade that follows, and Watch Tower directors are jailed under the Espionage Act in 1918.
Rutherford introduces the name Jehovah's witnesses at Columbus, Ohio (1931), and in 1933 about 20,000 Witnesses live in Nazi Germany, about 10,000 of whom are imprisoned.
Knorr becomes president (1942) and expands missionary activity and branch offices worldwide; the full New World Translation follows in 1961.
Publications build expectation of 1975; baptisms rise from about 59,000 (1966) to more than 297,000 (1974), and membership falls after the prediction fails.
Doctrinal authority passes from the president to the Governing Body (1976).
The Brooklyn property is sold in 2016 and operations are planned to move to Warwick (2017); in 2025 the denomination reports about 9 million publishers.
